newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end little changed before Fed meets.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end little changed before Fed meets.

text.p: Swiss shares ended a quiet session little changed on Monday ahead of the late afternoon release of Roche 1996 profit figures and Tuesday's decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve whether to raise U.S. interest rates.
Prices were bolstered by firming futures on government bonds and a favourable German share market. But profit taking put shares under pressure towards the end of the session.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index added 6.0 points, or 0.13 percent, to 4,497.3 points. The broad Swiss Performance Index rose 2.19 points, or 0.08 percent, to 2,856.83 points.

Roche said after the bourse closed that 1996 group net rose 16 percent to 3,899 million Swiss francs. Traders said this was at the lower end of expectations. One trader called the result "slightly disappointing".
Roche also proposed raising its dividend to 75 francs from 64 francs.
Most-active Roche certificates lost 85 francs to 12,250 before the news. Dealers said Roche results were likely to influence the bourse in the next few sessions.
Novartis registered shares ended up 11 francs to 1,714.
Nestle, which will release its 1996 results on Wednesday, added four francs to 1,571. Analysts' median forecast is for net profit to rise around 10 percent to 3.23 billion.
Among financials, attention focused on Credit Suisse Group, which gave up some of its intra-day gains to end one franc up at 166.50 francs.
ABB shares were up nine francs to 1,682 after it announced it was selling its refrigeration business to Denmark's Sabroe Regrigeration A/S for $93 million.
Insurers Swiss Re, Winterthur and Zurich were slightly lower.
Industrials Sulzer and Clariant were also among the day's losers.
Stocks of inspection firm Surveillance continued their recent decline, slumping 70 francs, or 2.26 percent, to 3,030 francs.
